specification_compliance: No invariants file exists for this change, so there is no declared list to check against and bucket A is unavailable.

The r3 finding keeponly-wipes-selection-on-list-reload is addressed by c2d901997. The pruning effect (FolderBrowser.tsx:620-625) now does nothing unless nameFilter.appliedText differs from prunedForTextRef. A reload leaves debouncedText unchanged, so the effect returns early (useFolderFilter.ts:72) whether or not `files` empties. useInfiniteScroll.reset (useInfiniteScroll.ts:124,127) sets items=[] and loading=true in the same batch, so the empty frame is also covered by the `loading` guard. The partial or stopped batch path (SelectionBar onSelectOnly + refresh) therefore keeps the failed ids. The Shift anchor is no longer nulled by reloads either, because keepOnly is not called.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Since c2d901997, a selected file that the filter comes to hide while the text stays the same stays selected while hidden. Examples are an inline rename to a non-matching name, or a websocket update after which the reloaded rows no longer match it. A later bulk action (trash, move, copy) would include it, and SelectionBar can show a count above totalCount. The test file's UNSPEC comment says 'a file the filter comes to hide leaves the selection'; only text-driven hiding does now. Relative to origin/develop this is not a regression, because the base never pruned.

If the filter text changes after a reload has brought back only page 1, matching selected files from later pages are dropped because they are not loaded. With no filter text change, they survive. Whether a selection should survive for files that are not loaded is not specified.
Pre-existing, unchanged: FolderBrowser toolbar `fileIds` and handlePlayAll / hasPlayableFiles (FolderBrowser.tsx:609-648) still read the unfiltered `files`.
regression_risks: prunedForTextRef is per FolderBrowser instance and is not reset on subject change (folder, sort, type). A text change in the same render as a subject change, before reset() runs in its effect (FolderBrowser.tsx:650-653 documents a loading:false frame with stale rows), would prune against the previous subject's rows. The two would have to coincide in one frame, so this is unlikely in normal use.
When a fetch fails (useInfiniteScroll.ts:106-112: items=[] and loading=false), changing the filter text then prunes the selection to empty. In that state no rows are shown anyway.
test_coverage: These are mutations I reasoned through; I did not run the tests. Removing the `loading ||` guard fails 'waits for a reload before pruning against newly typed text': the debounce fires while files=[], keepOnly([]) clears 'a', and the test expects 'a'.

Going back to row-keyed pruning (dropping the prunedForTextRef comparison, keeping the loading guard) fails 'keeps the selection when the list reloads under the filter': the reload with FILES.slice(0,2) gives visible [a], c is dropped, and the test expects 'a,c'.
Removing the anchor-null branch in keepOnly fails 'selects only the clicked row on Shift after the anchor was hidden'.
No test covers a selected row becoming hidden without a text change (rename or row update), so the behavior described in potential_unspecified_behavior is not pinned either way.
No useSelection unit test for keepOnly; it is covered only through the FolderBrowser integration tests, which mock useFolderFiles and never call the real reset().
not_verified: I did not run the test suite, the type checker, or the app; the analysis is a static read.
Not checked: whether selection is cleared on folder navigation (FolderBrowser.tsx:534, :812), which decides whether the subject-change frame matters.
Not checked: inline rename's exact flow, i.e. whether rename is reachable while a selection is active.
trajectory: r1 → r2 and r2 → r3 (a3c4b533b, ac9090203) are docs-only. r2 → r3 code (d5123d37d) added a stored-state reconciliation: an effect that prunes the selection with keepOnly, plus an anchor-reset branch in keepOnly. r3 → r4 (c2d901997) keeps that effect and patches its trigger. It removes the rows-keyed `isActive` condition, and adds a new piece of state (prunedForTextRef), a new branch (the `loading` guard), and a new field exposed from useFolderFilter (appliedText). It removes one condition but adds a ref and a guard on top of the effect the previous round introduced, so the design is being patched rather than replaced. be266cf97 is docs-only. The patch does close the r3 reload defect, and I found no new defect a user would hit in normal use.
